equity_bridge.note: Q2-2026 10-Q balance sheet, 2026-06-30. Their income is equity-accounted below operating income, so it is not in the EBITDA flows; the matching asset is added here (excluded-income/matching-asset rule). Book, not market -- Mekonomen is listed but the stake is small enough that book is adequate.
Q2-2026 10-Q balance sheet, 2026-06-30. Deducted once here; flows are consolidated.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr, rounded down; equity CAGR rejected as the anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (+6.3%) diverges from EPS 3yr CAGR (-17.2%) by far more than 30%. Book value grew because FY2023's $2.1bn debt-funded Uni-Select acquisition expanded the asset base and buybacks slowed to a trickle, while earnings fell from the FY2021-22 scrap/used-car-price peak. Equity CAGR is not a usable growth anchor here.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs end at FY2025 (continuing ops). Start points FY2022 (3yr) and FY2020 (5yr) are whole-company including Self Service (~$600m revenue, high-margin in the 2021-22 scrap-price spike), so the revenue CAGRs understate continuing-ops growth by ~1pp and the EPS/FCF CAGRs overstate the decline somewhat. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC): FY2020 1,242 -> FY2025 813; FY2022 990 -> FY2025 813. Owner-FCF CAGR (-8.1% 5yr) is slightly below reported (-7.8%) because SBC rose from $29m to $34m while FCF fell -- SBC is immaterial at 0.25% of revenue, so this is noise rather than a signal. The real story is that FCF has fallen every year since the FY2020-21 working-capital-release peak while revenue grew: margin compression (EBITDA 15.1% FY2020 -> 10.3% FY2025 on the reported series) plus the Uni-Select integration.

scenario_narratives.base: LKQ muddles through as a low-growth, cash-generative distributor. The German ERP disruption that forced the August 2026 guidance cut resolves over H2-2026/H1-2027, the $75m European cost program delivers, and North America keeps outgrowing a repairable-claims market that declines 1-3% a year. Revenue is flat-to-slightly-down in the year to June 2027 and then grows ~2-2.5% nominal (price and ADAS content offsetting unit declines). GAAP EBITDA margin recovers from 9.4-9.7% to 11% by year 5 and stays there, below FY2023-24. Capex normalises to 2%, acquired-intangible amortisation runs off, and the ~$3.7bn net debt is serviced from ~$0.8-1.0bn of unlevered FCF. No value is ascribed to the strategic review in this case.
scenario_narratives.bull: The bull axes are (1) claims stabilisation -- used-car values firming and insurance premiums easing mean fewer total losses, so repairable volumes stop falling; (2) Europe either fixed (margin lifted toward North America's) or sold at a multiple above where the group trades, with proceeds cutting leverage; (3) ADAS calibration (Elitek) and EV body-part salvage adding ~1pt of growth. Margins return to 12% (FY2023 level), growth runs 3-3.5% mid-horizon, terminal growth 2.5% and a 15x cap. A sale of the whole company at a control premium -- the activist (Ananym) thesis, with BofA/Goldman/Wachtell retained since January 2026 -- is one route to realising this value quickly, but the figure here is the fundamental value, not a bid.
scenario_narratives.bear: The bear axes are structural, not cyclical: ADAS-driven accident avoidance and rising total-loss rates shrink the repairable-claims pool every year; EV mix erodes the high-margin mechanical categories; tariffs on imported aftermarket parts are absorbed rather than passed through; Europe never earns its cost of capital and cannot be sold at a price that helps; and the strategic review ends without a deal, removing the floor the market has been pricing. Revenue falls 2% a year for two years, margin sits at 9%, growth is 1% thereafter at a 12x terminal cap. Leverage at ~3.6x (including operating leases) turns a modest EV decline into a large equity decline, which is why this scenario's value sits far below base despite positive cash flow throughout.

valuation_philosophy.summary: LKQ is valued as an unlevered owner-FCF stream from a mature, slowly shrinking distribution business, discounted at an 8% USD WACC with the cyclical and execution risks charged in the scenario paths and weights rather than the discount rate. GAAP EBITDA is used, with the perennial restructuring charges treated as a real cost. Operating leases are an operating cost (ASC 842), so they are inside EBITDA and outside net debt. The share count is held flat because SBC (0.25% of revenue) is fully expensed; the house/street band is correspondingly narrow. The strategic alternatives review (announced 2026-01-26, no deadline, no deal nine months on) is treated as optionality on top of the fundamental value: it supports a 20% bull weight that the operating evidence alone would not, but no takeout premium is baked into the base case and no deal-completes/deal-breaks weighting is used because there is no offer to weight. The base year is TTM to June 2026 against the June 2026 balance sheet, so year 1 is the twelve months to June 2027.
key_risks_to_valuation: Repairable-claims decline is structural (ADAS, total-loss rates) and runs faster than the 1-3%/yr the base assumes -- the single biggest driver of the bear/base gap
German ERP disruption and European margin recovery slip into 2027 or beyond; the $75m cost program does not land
Tariffs on Taiwan/China/Mexico-sourced aftermarket parts compress gross margin if pass-through is incomplete
Leverage: $3.66bn net debt plus $1.38bn operating leases (~3.6x EBITDA) means every 1pt of EBITDA margin is worth roughly $4-5/share of equity
Strategic review ends with no transaction, or sells Europe at a price that reduces rather than creates value; conversely a sale of the whole company would cap the upside at the bid

Terminal assumptions: the 14x FCF cap binds in the base case; at a 12x cap (bear) or a 15x cap (bull) the value moves materially, so the exit multiple a buyer grants a declining distributor is a judgment the reader should test on the Assumptions sheet
Restructuring charges are treated as recurring; if management's 'Segment EBITDA' basis is right and they genuinely end, GAAP margins would be ~0.7pt higher than modelled

inputs.base_revenue_basis: TTM to 2026-06-30, continuing operations (FY2025 13,651 - H1-2025 6,840 + H1-2026 6,877). Self Service (Pick Your Part) was sold Oct-2025 and is in discontinued operations; FY2023-FY2025 and all 2026 periods in the Metrics CSV are already restated continuing-ops. FY2022 and earlier are whole-company and NOT comparable (Self Service was ~$600m revenue).
inputs.share_count_basis: 253.0m common shares on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (2026-07-23, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus the 0.1m basic-to-diluted gap in the Q2-2026 weighted average (254.6m basic / 254.7m diluted). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice. Buybacks ($159m FY2025, $53m H1-2026) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL cash-flow add-back, TTM to 2026-06-30 (FY2025 $34m - H1-2025 $17m + H1-2026 $18m). LKQ publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure; equity-award tax withholding has not been tagged since FY2019 and ran $0.4-7.6m/yr in FY2014-FY2018, so it is immaterial at ~0.05% of revenue and is not added. SBC is 0.26% of revenue -- the house/street band is narrow for this name.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM to 2026-06-30: FY2025 $159m - H1-2025 $79m + H1-2026 $53m. Pace has slowed sharply from $1.04bn (FY2022) as leverage rose; ~$1.5bn of the $4.5bn authorization remains but authorized is not spent. Dividends ($1.20/share, ~$305m/yr) are a distribution of the unlevered flows modelled here and are not deducted.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.2 -> cost of equity ~10.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.7% (FY2025 interest expense $224m on ~$3.9bn average debt), after-tax ~4.2%. Capital structure at market: equity $5.77bn (253.1m x $22.78) vs debt $3.96bn -> 41% debt. WACC = 0.59 x 10.2% + 0.41 x 4.2% = 7.7%, rounded up to 8.0%. The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality, the European execution risk and the claims-decline risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost, as US GAAP ASC 842 already presents them: operating lease cost ($344m FY2025) is inside operating expenses and so inside the GAAP EBITDA the margin path is anchored to, and operating lease payments ($347m FY2025) are inside operating cash flow. Operating lease liabilities ($1,380m at 2026-06-30) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. Finance leases ($125m) are inside total_debt as the filer reports them (DebtAndCapitalLeaseObligations). Sanity multiples must be lease-consistent: EV ex-operating-leases against post-ASC-842 EBITDA is the matching pair here (the leases are a cost in EBITDA, not a liability in EV).
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interest is $24m at 2026-06-30 and NCI's share of profit is not separately tagged (immaterial). Deducted once, in the equity bridge, at book. Flows are modelled on consolidated GAAP EBITDA.
inputs.ebitda_basis: GAAP operating income + D&A (the CSV EBITDA column), continuing operations. This is BELOW LKQ's own 'Segment EBITDA' because restructuring charges (recurring every year since 2019: 1 LKQ Europe, the 2024-2026 global restructuring, the $75m European cost program) and the FY2025 $52m goodwill impairment are left in as real costs. TTM Jun-2026 GAAP EBITDA is $1,284m (9.4%); $1,336m (9.8%) ex the goodwill impairment. Management's FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $2.60-2.90 (midpoint $2.75 x ~255m = ~$700m adjusted NI) back-solves to roughly 10.2% on a GAAP-style EBITDA basis before restructuring, which is why the base path recovers from 9.7% toward 10.2% in year 2 rather than starting there.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, cyclical industrial'; adaptations file read for leases, NCI and risk-once). LKQ is an operating distributor with real, if shrinking, free cash flow; it is not a holdco, REIT or bank, and the strategic review has produced no transaction, so a deal-completes/deal-breaks frame would be weighting a price nobody has offered. The three scenarios are fundamental paths; the review's optionality is discussed in valuation_philosophy and the bull narrative, not baked into the base case. BASE YEAR: the balance sheet is 2026-06-30 and the flows are TTM to that date, so year 1 is the twelve months to June 2027 (not calendar FY2026), discounted one full period from the valuation date; this is the only internally consistent pairing for a December filer valued in October with a June balance sheet. last_fcf ($590m) is the reported LEVERED owner FCF (OCF - capex - SBC, after ~$215m of cash interest) and is an anchor for the reader; the engine's projected FCF is UNLEVERED (built from EBITDA, interest handled through WACC and the net-debt bridge), so the component year-1 FCF (~$800m) sits above last_fcf by roughly after-tax interest, as it should. Cross-check: FY2026 levered FCF guidance of $625-775m + ~$160m after-tax interest = ~$785-935m unlevered, bracketing the year-1 build. Price: regular close of the prior day, not after-hours; 52-week range 21.17-37.13, so the stock sits near the bottom of its range after the August guidance cut.

bear.rationale: Structural decline: ADAS keeps cutting accident frequency and total-loss rates keep rising, so North American repairable claims fall 2-4%/yr for several more years; the German ERP recovery drags into 2027; tariffs on Taiwan/China/Mexico-sourced aftermarket parts are only partly passed through; the strategic review concludes without a transaction. Margin stuck at 9%, revenue shrinks for three years then crawls at 1%. Terminal cap 12x for a business in managed decline. Leverage (3.6x including leases) means the equity absorbs all of it, but the flows stay comfortably positive -- this is not a solvency scenario, and the bear does not reach the zero-TV floor.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (to Jun-2027) -0.5%: FY2026 organic guidance is -3% to -1% with H1-2026 already printed at +0.5% reported (FX-aided), so H2-2026 runs ~-2% organic and H1-2027 recovers modestly as the German ERP disruption laps. Years 2-9 ramp to 2.5% nominal: ~2% parts inflation and rising ADAS/calibration content per repair, against a continuing 1-3%/yr decline in repairable claims; no European bolt-on M&A assumed. Terminal 2.0%.
base.margin_rationale: GAAP EBITDA (restructuring and impairments left in). TTM Jun-2026 is 9.4% (9.8% ex the $52m goodwill impairment); year 1 at 9.7% carries the ERP cost into H2-2026. Recovery to 11.0% by year 5 assumes the $75m European cost program lands (+0.5pt), the ERP disruption ends, and North America holds its ~16-17% segment margin. 11.0% is still below FY2024 (11.2%) and well below FY2023 (12.4%): no return to the 2021-22 scrap-price margins.
base.da_capex_rationale: D&A 3.0% of revenue (FY2025 $418m: $226m depreciation + $183m amortisation of acquired intangibles) glides to 2.3% as the Uni-Select/Rhiag/Keystone intangibles run off. Capex 1.8% rising to 2.0% (FY2025 $216m was a trough at 1.6%; FY2023-24 ran 2.3-2.7%; FY2026 guidance implies ~$200-250m). D&A above capex throughout is the intangible-amortisation tax shield, which shrinks as the gap closes.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid / GAAP operating income: FY2023 23%, FY2024 28%, FY2025 30% (the FY2025 figure carries tax on the Self Service gain); GAAP effective rate 25.5%. 27% flat on EBIT blends US federal+state and the European mix.
base.wc_rationale: Distributor: inventory ~$3.0bn (22% of revenue) + receivables ~$1.1bn against payables ~$1.5bn, so net working capital is ~20% of revenue and growth consumes cash. -20% of each year's revenue change; negative growth in year 1 releases a little cash, as FY2020 showed.

bull.rationale: Repairable claims stabilise (firming used-car values and easing insurance premiums, as management cited in Q2-2026), Europe is fixed or sold and the group margin returns to the FY2023 level of ~12%. Growth 3-3.5% in years 3-5 from ADAS calibration, EV salvage partnerships and modest European consolidation. Same WACC: the upside is in the flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: two guidance cuts inside a year, a chronic European underperformer now compounded by an ERP failure, structural (not cyclical) repairable-claims decline, tariff exposure the company cannot fully pass through, and 3.6x lease-inclusive leverage that makes the equity a levered bet on a declining core. Bull cut from 35% to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right (claims stabilise AND Europe is fixed or sold AND margins recover 2.5pt); the live strategic review is the main reason it is not lower -- a sale of Europe or the whole company at a control premium would deliver bull-case value without the operational turnaround, but no transaction has been announced in nine months and the house rule is not to pay for a bid that does not exist. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
